<!--
  What an issue needs from the person who found the defect.

  The template is short on purpose. anvil is built on the idea that a report is worth
  exactly as much as the evidence in it, so the questions here are the ones that turn
  "something looked wrong" into a reproduction the maintainer can run.
-->

## What happened

<!--
  One or two sentences. What did you run, what did you expect, what happened instead?
  "anvil doctor crashed" is a start; "anvil doctor crashed on a repo with a package.json
  but no lockfile" is a report.
-->

## Reproduction

<!--
  The smallest command sequence that shows it, and the output you got. A repository or
  fixture is better than a description.
-->

```
```

## Environment

<!-- `anvil version` prints the version and the JSON schema version. -->

- anvil version:
- Node version: <!-- `node --version` -->
- OS: <!-- windows / macos / linux -->
- Repository: <!-- the repository you ran it in, or a minimal example -->

## Verification

<!--
  Say what you ran and what it printed. A report with no output is a hypothesis, and the
  first thing a maintainer does with a hypothesis is run it.
-->

- [ ] I ran a command and pasted the output
- [ ] This is a documentation or wording problem, not a defect

## Notes

<!--
  Anything that is not obvious from the rest: a workaround, a piece of information you
  could not find, or the fact that you could not reproduce it at all. The last one is
  worth saying out loud.
-->
